Usage: gwt remove <target> ... [flags]

Remove checkouts and their branches, keeping a recovery ref for anything discarded.

Runs without prompting. Several targets form one batch, and a failed target
does not stop the others.

Always refused: the main checkout, the one you are in, a locked one, and one that
holds another worktree. Refused unless --discard-dirty: uncommitted, untracked or
index-hidden changes, or a status that cannot be read. Refused unless --force or
--keep-branch: a branch not merged into the trunk, judged after fetching a remote
trunk that no fetch has reached within fetch.max_age, so a pull request merged
minutes ago counts. gwt list's removable applies the same rules. A target whose
commit or changes moved while gwt checked it is refused; stop any process still
working in a checkout before removing it.

Nothing is discarded without a recovery ref under refs/wt-trash/<batch>/: the
snapshot --discard-dirty takes (shaped like a stash: first parent HEAD, second a
commit of the index, ignored files left out), the tip --force deletes, or a
removed detached checkout's HEAD. Restore one with git branch <name> <ref>. Refs
older than recovery.keep expire on each removal. Ignored files go with the
checkout, which moves to <worktree_root>/.trash and is deleted in the background.

Text: what was removed and any ref kept, on stdout; each failed target on stderr
as "gwt: error: <target>: <reason>". The command exits 1 when any target failed.

Arguments:
  <target> ...                A branch (its registered checkout, or the branch alone when it has
                              none) or a checkout path, absolute or starting with ./, which reaches
                              detached checkouts.

Flags:
      --force                 Delete a branch that is not merged into the trunk; its tip is kept as
                              a recovery ref.
      --discard-dirty         Remove a checkout that holds changes, after snapshotting them to a
                              recovery ref.
      --keep-branch           Remove only the checkout and keep its branch, so no merge verdict is
                              needed.
      --expect-head=COMMIT    Refuse unless the one target is still at COMMIT. Pass the commit you
                              judged, so work committed since cannot be lost.
      --json                  Print one JSON object per target, one per line, instead of text.

Inherited flags:
  -h, --help                  Show context-sensitive help.

JSON:
  One object per line, one per target, in order, success or not; a failure is
  also reported on stderr:
    ok                true when everything asked for this target was done
    target            the target as given
    path              the checkout; absent for a branch without one
    branch            the branch; "" for a detached checkout
    worktree_removed  true once the checkout is gone, even when a later step failed
    branch_deleted    true when the branch was deleted
    recovery_ref      the ref keeping what was discarded; absent when nothing was
    error             why the target failed; absent on success
  With worktree_removed true, branch_deleted false and an error, the checkout is
  gone and its branch remains: inspect the branch before deleting it by hand.

The trunk and merge verdicts:
  The trunk is where work lands: the first of origin/HEAD, origin/main,
  origin/master, main and master that exists, else the main checkout's branch. It
  is not create's base, which only says where a new branch forks from.

  A branch is merged into the trunk when the trunk contains its commits, when one
  trunk commit carries its combined change (a squash merge), or when trunk commits
  carry each of its commits' changes (a rebase). A change match also needs a clean
  merge that leaves the trunk's contents exactly as they are. A branch with merge
  commits of its own, or whose lines the trunk edited again later, may stay
  unconfirmed. A branch with no commits of its own counts as merged: it holds
  nothing to lose.

Exit codes:
  0    success
  1    failed, or a creation was declined; remove and merged also exit 1 when any target failed,
       after printing every target's result
  2    invalid arguments; nothing was run
